final_answer: Lowering corporate tax rates may not boost long-term job growth because companies might reinvest savings into share buybacks or dividends rather than hiring. Tax cuts could also incentivize profit shifting, reducing taxable income while avoiding capital expenditures. Additionally, if tax cuts are temporary, firms may delay investments, anticipating future rate changes. Global competition means rivals might match cuts, diluting potential benefits. Furthermore, reduced government revenue could lead to cuts in public services that support job creation. Historical data shows mixed results, with many tax cuts failing to significantly increase employment. Structural factors like automation and globalization also influence job markets more than tax rates alone.
